title: The Majesty of Calmness
author: William George Jordan
hook: You try to hold in your anger when people insult you at work.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You try to hold in your anger when people insult you at work. William George Jordan wrote a century ago that self-control gives you power over every situation. In 2011, psychologist Brad Bushman at Ohio State University tested how people deal with anger. He found that venting your anger actually makes you about twice as aggressive as staying silent. What did the researchers find when people simply paused? Pausing lowers your heart rate and calms your brain down instantly. Other studies on emotion regulation show this same effect, which scientists call the cognitive reappraisal strategy. So why do you still want to yell back? Your brain confuses temporary emotional release with actual problem solving. The result? Remaining quiet is not weak, it is your strongest defense. That's it. So next time someone tries to push your buttons, remember how to act when you try to hold in your anger.

claims.claim: Venting anger increases aggression compared to distraction or quiet waiting, while pausing lowers physiological arousal.
Self-control and emotional composure act as the ultimate sources of personal energy and mastery.
